- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.30) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.40), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for risk reversal.  
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward spikes in sentiment; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 2–3 periods after spike.  
- Mean reversion is evident in 3–5 period horizons: if forecast is > 2σ above recent mean, reduce by 1–2% per period until convergence.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven momentum; weight sentiment index (last 5 days) as 20% multiplier to adjust forecast baseline.  
- If sentiment turns sharply positive after a negative trend, model tends to lag; add 1–2% to forecast 1–2 periods ahead to capture sentiment shift.
